{{Quote|We will not fight them at all. We would rather die than to kill others.|Tee Watt Kaa|<ref name="Defenders of Peace">{{TCW|Defenders of Peace}}</ref>}}
'''Tee Watt Kaa''' was the leader of the [[Lurmen/Legends|Lurmen]] on the planet [[Maridun/Legends|Maridun]].

==Biography==

===Escaping from the War===
An advocate of the pacisfist [[Te Padka/Legends|philosophy of Te Padka]],<ref name=":3">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref> Tee Watt Kaa led his people on a journey away<ref name=":0" /> from [[Mygeeto/Legends|Mygeeto]]<ref name=":3" />  to escape the bloodshed and violence of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="SWE-Lurmen" /> They eventually landed<ref name=":0" /> on the uncharted world<ref name="SWE-Lurmen">{{SWE|groups|lurmen|Lurmen}}</ref> of [[Maridun/Legends|Maridun]] and encountered the vicious [[Amani/Legends|Amani]] people. Despite fruitless attempts to make peace with the natives, Kaa stayed true to his [[Te Padka/Legends|peaceful ideals]] and jettisoned an escape pod with his people, so the Amani could claim the ship like they wanted.<ref name=":0">''[[The Clone Wars: Neighbors]]''</ref>

After a while, the Lurmen gathered up giant pods from the local trees and fashioned a village out of them.<ref name=":2" /> Kaa had imagined that his son [[Wag Too/Legends|Wag Too]] would had followed in his footsteps, learning the lessons of [[Te Padka/Legends|Te Padka]] and leading the Lurmen colony when his time had past.<ref name=":3" />

===Defense of Maridum===
[[File:Tee_Watt_Aayla_tea.png|thumb|left|250x250px|Tee Watt Kaa offers tea to General Aayla Secura.]]There Kaa and his people lived in relative peace until approached by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]], [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]] and [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Bly/Legends|Bly]] after their crash landing. He initially refused to help General [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] due to his belief that the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] were perpetuators of the war, because they continued to fight in it. Eventually, Secura wore him down and he agreed to sent his son and healer [[Wag Too/Legends|Wag Too]] to help them, although she had to remain behind as collateral.<ref name=":1">{{TCW|Jedi Crash}}</ref> Through a series of conversations with the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]], the two became amiable and began to come to an understanding with each other.<ref name=":0" />

Much to the frustration of Ahsoka and Rex, Tee Watt Kaa refused to allow his people to form a resistance against a Separatist invasion force, even when the Separatists intended to exterminate them as a means to demonstrate the effectiveness of a new weapon. Tee Watt Kaa would not be convinced otherwise, as he was prepared to turn himself and his entire species into martyrs and victims of genocide just to prove his point. Although Ahsoka was reluctant to aid a people who she viewed as lacking in courage or the common sense to accept help, Anakin and Aayla were adamant about preventing the annihilation of innocents, regardless of their personal beliefs.<ref name=":2">{{TCW|Defenders of Peace}}</ref>

When the Separatists attacked the village, the Jedi and clone troopers engaged them in [[Defense of Maridun/Legends|battle]]. During the battle, Wag Too couldn't stand by any longer and, to his father's dismay, led a force of Lurmen into the battle. The Jedi and Lurmen successfully drove the Separatists off. Although Tee Watt Kaa did manage to display his gratitude for the survival of his people, he nevertheless wondered what the price was for Republic assistance. Seconds after he voiced this, three [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class]] [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] entered the Maridun world's atmosphere<ref name=":2" /> - a symbol of the dreaded [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] soon to come.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith">{{Film|III}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|My father is very strong willed and set in tradition.|Wag Too|<ref name="Defenders of Peace" />}}
Tee Watt Kaa was extremely devoted to the traditions of his people and a strict pacifist.<ref name=":2" /> Realistic enough to recognize dissention was a common element in life, he nonetheless believed in seeking out non-violent solutions. He refused to wield any weapon, even in self-defense.<ref name="TWK" /> He cared greatly for such ideals, and firmly believed the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] was no better than the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]] because the two were equally responsible for the war. He also believed because the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] fought and killed others they could not be called peacekeepers.<ref name=":1" /> Nevertheless, he was willing to help the injured if asked for it. As far as he was concerned, his people would rather die than engage in battle and he thought that if they sacrificed their beliefs, they were no better than the Separatists or the Republic. [[Wag Too/Legends|Wag Too]] rebelled against him in order to protect his home despite his father forbidding him to fight the Separatists.<ref name=":2" />

Tee Watt Kaa could also be sarcastic at times, telling [[Lok Durd/Legends|Lok Durd]] that his village was "an obvious threat" when it clearly wasn't.<ref name=":2" /> He was also indifferent to the Jedi<ref name=":1" /> and it was only after the Separatists were defeated that he finally admitted that he owed them thanks. But even then, he still wondered, "At what cost?"<ref name=":2" />

==Behind the scenes==
Tee Watt Kaa first appeared in the thirteenth episode of [[The Clone Wars: Season One|season one]] of ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'', "[[Jedi Crash]]," and was voiced by [[George Coe]].<ref name=":1" />

He also appeared in ''[[LEGO Star Wars III: The Clone Wars]]'' where he was given a [[Whip (weapon)|whip]] as weapon.<ref name="LEGO Star Wars III: The Clone Wars">''[[LEGO Star Wars III: The Clone Wars]]''</ref>
